paper_name: Physics-informed neural network for lithium-ion battery degradation stable modeling and prognosis

reproduction_mode.reason: The original raw experimental datasets, exact train/validation/test battery identities for the 10-cell synthetic setting, exact learning rate, epochs, learning-rate schedule, early stopping, and complete PDE equation implementation details are not fully available from the supplied materials. Therefore the plan reproduces the reported input-output structure, engineered feature space, PINN family, and executable training/evaluation pipeline using explicit synthetic-data and training assumptions.
what_is_reproduced: cell-level train/validation/test split at 6/2/2 using exactly 10 cells
test RMSE, test R2, and SOH true-versus-predicted plot generation
what_is_not_reproduced: raw voltage/current/time feature extraction unless explicitly implemented

task.target_formula: SOH = current available capacity / initial capacity

model.primary_model_name: Physics-informed neural network for battery SOH estimation

paper_understanding.paper_reported_training_protocol: Use 16 extracted features and cycle/time as model inputs; normalize features to [-1, 1]; train a PINN with data loss, monotonicity loss, and PDE/degradation-equation loss; split batteries approximately 6:2:2 for regular experiments; repeat experiments 10 times; Adam optimizer is reported in supplementary material; batch size is reported as 256 for XJTU and 512 for TJU/MIT/HUST.
important_notes: The paper extracts voltage-window features from V in [V_end - 0.2, V_end].
Supplementary material specifies XJTU/TJU voltage range [4.0, 4.2] V and MIT/HUST voltage range [3.4, 3.6] V.
The paper extracts current-window features from current between 0.5 A and 0.1 A during constant-voltage charging.
The paper's PINN contains F(.) for the feature/cycle-to-SOH mapping and G(.) for degradation dynamics.
Transfer learning freezes G(.) and fine-tunes F(.), but transfer learning is not used in the default executable reproduction.

selected_reproduction_strategy.selection_rule: Use primary_features as the default model input features.
selected_reproduction_strategy.reason: The paper reports 16 extracted current/voltage statistical features plus cycle/time as PINN inputs. Chemistry and protocol metadata are useful for synthetic variability but are not reported as direct model inputs, so they are generated as secondary features and excluded by default.

chemistry_assignment.note: In feature-level synthetic mode, chemistry controls metadata/statistical offsets rather than raw electrochemical simulation.

cycle_soh_generation.formula_template: soh = initial_soh - a * normalized_cycle - b * max(0, normalized_cycle - knee)^2 + noise
constraints: SOH should generally decrease with cycle_index
different cells must not have identical degradation trajectories
cycle_index must be integer starting at 1 for each cell

feature_generation.feature_value_formula_template: feature_raw = cell_offset + trend_strength * capacity_loss + nonlinear_strength * capacity_loss^2 + cycle_strength * normalized_cycle + chemistry_offset + noise; final model features are min-max scaled to [-1, 1] using train-set feature min/max

paper_feature_formula_reference.paper_current_window: I between 0.5 A and 0.1 A during constant-voltage charging

solution_network_F.description: Approximates f(t_i, x_i) mapping cycle/features to SOH.

dynamics_network_G.description: Approximates g(.) degradation dynamics term from SOH, cycle, and selected latent derivatives.

paper_basis: The paper reports F(.) and G(.) as small fully connected neural networks.
Supplementary snippets show Linear+Sin and Linear layers for PINN/MLP structures, but not enough complete context to guarantee exact implementation in this 10-cell synthetic setting.

executable_loss.total_loss_formula: L = L_data + alpha * L_mono + beta * L_pde

L_mono.implementation: Use torch.autograd.grad on scaled cycle_index input. Penalize positive derivative because degradation SOH should not increase with cycle.

L_pde.implementation: Compute d_soh_pred_d_cycle with autograd; pass constructed dynamics inputs through G; penalize mismatch.

batch_size.paper_reported_context: reported for XJTU; synthetic 10-cell reproduction adopts this value

validation_plan.validation_split: cell-level validation set containing cell_007 and cell_008

testing_plan.test_split: cell-level test set containing cell_009 and cell_010

evidence.text: The SOH of a battery is defined as the ratio of the current available capacity to the initial capacity.
For the current data, we choose the data with the current between 0.5 A and 0.1 A during the constant voltage charging.
Define the charge cut-off voltage of a battery as V_end, and the voltage data whose value is within [V_end-0.2, V_end] V is selected.
The mean, standard deviation, kurtosis, skewness, charging time, accumulated charge, curve slope, and curve entropy from the selected current and voltage curves, respectively ... are extracted.
The extracted 16 features and time (cycle) are used as inputs of the proposed PINN to estimate SOH.
The min–max normalization is performed on the features. That is, all features are scaled to the range [−1,1].

The proposed PINN consists of a solution function f(·) mapping features to SOH and a nonlinear function g(·) modeling battery degradation dynamics; f(·) and g(·) are replaced by small fully connected neural networks F(·) and G(·).
The training losses are described as data term loss L_data, monotonicity loss L_mono, and PDE loss L_PDE constrained by the degradation equation.
Training batteries, validation batteries, and test batteries were divided approximately in the ratio of 6:2:2.
MAPE is the mean absolute percentage error, and RMSE is the root mean square error.
Supplementary Note 2 gives formulas for mean, standard deviation, kurtosis, skewness, charging time, accumulated charge, curve slope, and entropy.
The proposed PINN was learned by minimizing the loss defined in Equation (9) of the Manuscript File, and the Adam optimizer was used in the training phase.

The trade-off parameters alpha and beta are set to 0.7 and 20 for XJTU battery dataset, 1 and 50 for TJU and MIT datasets, and 0.5 and 80 for HUST dataset. Batch size is 256 for XJTU and 512 for other datasets.
